decision: continue only with a real shared-context workload before additional architecture or training work

zero_decoding_efficiency.large_batch_observation: Successful batch-32/64 speedups are 1.23x to 1.66x; 4B batch-64 generation is memory-limited while label-logit completes.

technical_conclusion: Larger Qwen3 base models naturally develop a materially more stable zero-decoding label-logit interface, although residual position sensitivity remains.
Autoregressive decoding is not required for competitive multiple-choice decisions in this setup and imposes substantial latency and KV-memory cost.
The systems advantage is workload-dependent: it is largest at low batch size and narrows when shared prefill dominates.
Standard KV branching can reuse a long prompt prefix profitably for larger models, but BF16 segmented-attention numerics can flip near-tied small-model decisions.
A dedicated semantic decision head was not justified by the Route A gate; it remains an untested alternative rather than a demonstrated improvement.
next_required_evidence: A dataset with genuine shared context and multiple independent decision questions, plus a numerically controlled shared-state implementation, is required before claiming a general Jev-like architecture benefit.
